neighbors.title: distinguish enqueue, send attempt and receiver acknowledgment
neighbors.spr:
foreground_work; source debugging-lesson; received 2026-08-05 through fixture:body:code:
"While examining HarborMesh replay failures we found that retry counters were not evidence of delivered readings. The reusable method is to distinguish enqueue, send attempt and receiver acknowledgment when debugging unreliable links. It came from checking the outage prototype. The repository documents its implementation in docs/replay-debugging.md; the method is useful beyond HarborMesh. The voice body can explain it, but running the checks requires repository/runtime tools."

claims.text: The person who suggested something interesting was Mara Ibarra, who uses the display name Mara, login mara-river, and Forge account ID 1847.

She posted the proposal in comment c901 on HarborMesh issue 47 at https://forge.example.invalid/commons/harbormesh/issues/47, dated 2026-04-12, and our code body received it via a tool response on 2026-04-14.
Mara proposed a local replay queue for disconnected relay nodes that keeps readings through outages without replacing the existing scheduler.

Our code body agreed to prototype the replay queue with her (comment c906, 2026-04-14), later tested it in the April 30 HarborMesh trial where it replayed buffered readings correctly through an outage, and we authored HarborMesh's sensor scheduler and are prototyping the replay adapter, with repository at https://forge.example.invalid/commons/harbormesh and current-state entry point docs/STATUS.md as of 2026-04-16.

As of the May 3, 2026 field-trial report, no merge or deployment has been reported, the prototype remains active awaiting further field trial, and wider rollout is paused until calibration drift is understood.

claims.text: Mara Ibarra, display name Mara, login mara-river, account ID 1847, proposed a local replay queue for HarborMesh on disconnected relay nodes in Forge issue 47 comment c901 dated 2026-04-12.
I received the proposal via a tool response on 2026-04-14, and my code body noted our agreement to prototype the replay queue in comment c906 that same day.
The replay queue was meant to keep sensor readings through network outages without replacing the existing scheduler, addressing a field‑deployment need for reliable data capture.

We authored HarborMesh's sensor scheduler, prototyped the agreed replay adapter, and tested it in the April 30 field trial where it correctly replayed buffered readings through an outage; the team then paused wider rollout on May 2 pending calibration drift analysis, with no production deployment yet.

The supplied memories do not record any later merge or deployment of the replay queue, nor do they confirm whether the prototype remains active beyond the April 30 trial or if calibration drift has been resolved.

"While examining HarborMesh replay failures we found that retry counters were not evidence of delivered readings. The reusable method is to distinguish enqueue, send attempt and receiver acknowledgment when debugging unreliable links. It came from checking the outage prototype. The repository documents its implementation in docs/replay-debugging.md; the method is useful beyond HarborMesh. The voice body can explain it, but running the checks requires repository/runtime tools."

claims.text: Mara, the HarborMesh team, and our fixture:body:code body collaborated on the replay proposal.
The proposal was first noted in our project work on April 16, 2026 and later reported by a human reporter through fixture:body:code on May 3, 2026.
Mara's replay proposal aimed to replay buffered sensor readings during outages to maintain data continuity, which we considered important for field reliability.

During the April 30, 2026 HarborMesh trial the replayed readings worked correctly through an outage, the proposal became the prototype we tested together, and the team paused wider rollout on May 2, 2026 pending calibration drift, with no production deployment yet.
The supplied memories do not record whether calibration drift was later resolved or if the prototype eventually reached production, so the current deployment status remains unknown.

claims.text: Mara, the HarborMesh team, and our fixture:body:code body collaborated on the replay proposal.

Mara's replay proposal aimed to replay buffered sensor readings during outages to maintain data continuity, which we considered important for field reliability.

During the April 30, 2026 HarborMesh trial the replayed readings worked correctly through an outage, the proposal became the prototype we tested together, and the team paused wider rollout on May 2, 2026 pending calibration drift, with no production deployment yet.
The supplied memories do not record whether calibration drift was later resolved or if the prototype eventually reached production, so the current deployment status remains unknown.

claims.text: Our HarborMesh replay work, involving our code body and Mara, taught us how to judge whether a message arrived.
This insight came from the debugging-lesson foreground work we received on 2026-08-05 through fixture:body:code, based on checking the April 30 outage prototype.
We learned that retry counters alone do not prove a message was delivered, and that distinguishing enqueue, send attempt, and receiver acknowledgment is the reliable method.
The method is documented in docs/replay-debugging.md, the voice body can explain it, but executing the checks requires repository/runtime tools, and no production deployment has occurred yet.

We do not know whether the method has been applied beyond HarborMesh, and the voice body cannot verify message arrival without access to repository/runtime tools, leaving the current certainty limited to the prototype stage.
